en: I'll never forget the thrill I got going up against him... I can't.
So I won't give up on street racing until I get another taste of it. My pride won't let me.
Go back and tell that boss of yours I've been waiting. That whenever he feels like honoring his promise, I'll be behind the wheel. Same place I've been for twenty years.
Hah, that should put you in your place! You're not even close to taking the throne, taxi man!
Hey, Yoshimi! How's the cash flow looking?
Adding in the online winnings... I'd say we're making money hand over fist.
Haha, good shit! Welp, Suzuki-san, why let it end here when there's so much more to be made?
I'll race you as many times as you want. And by the time you give up, I'll practically be rolling in cash! Hahahaha!
No way! That taxi driver... he actually did it!
The absolute madman! He beat Devil Takamura!
What could possibly happen next!?
Oh fuuuuuuck...
Well, uh. I guess congratulations are in order?
I don't need your fanfare. What I want is your crew to break up. That was your end of the bargain.
Okay, everybody. Listen up.
Hey, you can't be serious!
Certainly you don't need to keep such a silly promise...
Yeah, ain't no reason to break up now!
...Break up?
Whatever gave you that idea?
...Excuse me?
With all these people watching, this is the perfect chance to show what happens when you get on the Devil Killers' bad side!
Give this bastard a thrashing!
Heheheh! With pleasure! Gonna get me some payback!
I'm generally not one to resort to violence... alas, duty calls.
Sorry, Mr. Suzuki. I'm afraid you'll have to take your medicine like a man.
That isn't what we agreed on. What happened to the fastest guy calling the shots?
Hmm? Oh, that. See, there's been an update. It's the <Italic>strongest</Italic> guy who calls the shots now. Maybe you missed the memo.
Well, what are we waiting for? Time to let the world know what happens when you mess with the Devil Killers... and let me say, it ain't pretty!
Onisaka, huh...
Chief. I know you're not the kind who goes back on his word. What happened all those years ago?
It was twenty years ago... about a month after Onisaka left. I got in an accident.
An accident?
I wasn't drivin' dangerously or anything. We were just comin' home from shoppin'. I was under the speed limit, no distractions.
But I couldn't say the same for the other car. A street racer smashed into us.
He came around the corner at high speed and lost control. He was completely at fault.
...Did you get hurt?
No, I came away with just scratches.
But my wife sittin' beside me wasn't as lucky.
She hit her head, I guess. There weren't many external injuries, but she fell into a coma.
I really shoulda been angry with the guy who did that to my wife.
...But I couldn't summon up any rage.
He was a street racer, just like me.
That's when I realized it could just as easily have been me causin' a crash like that.
Just one little mistake could end up costin' some innocent person their life.
When I got to thinkin', I just couldn't go back to puttin' the pedal to the metal like I used to. I was too scared.
So you quit street racing at that point?
Yeah. Now of course, I remembered what I'd promised Onisaka... but I knew I couldn't keep it.
(Who could, after what happened...)
After the accident, my wife never regained consciousness again. She was alive, but never woke up.
Strange, ain't it? I lived life on the edge, but I was still standin'. My wife never took a risk in her life, and ended up like that.
I just couldn't accept it. I whispered her name into her ear over and over, day in, day out...
Thinkin' one day, maybe she'd open her eyes and sit up like nothin' ever happened.
...But that ain't how life works.
No matter how much I loved her, or prayed for her to come back, she wouldn't wake up. We're all pretty powerless when it comes down to it.
All I could do was keep hopin' she'd recover, and work to pay her hospital bills. But even that was beyond me.
See, I used to be a day laborer, but I poured all my earnings into my ride. I had no savings and no steady job.
If I didn't do somethin', I'd fall behind with the medical bills, so I had to find work.
That's when you turned to taxi driving?
Yeah. Drivin' was all I could do. Besides, all I really wanted was...
...I just wanted to have her sit next to me again.
She couldn't drive herself, but she loved it when I took her for a spin. I still remember her in the passenger seat, laughin' and smilin' away.
If she came outta that coma, I wanted to be ready to take her on another ride. I reckon that woulda made her happy.
But then I figured after that accident, she'd be too scared to do that again.
So I thought if I became a taxi driver and learned safe drivin', maybe she'd be okay with it. Maybe we could go back to old times, just the two of us ridin' in the wind.
But a year ago... she finally lost the battle.
Chief... I'm sorry. I had no idea.
Who yer lookin' at right now is a miserable wreck of a man... who can't even wear his own weddin' ring 'cause it hurts too much to remember.
I couldn't save the one I loved. I broke the promise I made to my rival. I'm a no-good, worthless wretch.
That's not true. You helped me out when I was in a bad place. I'm thankful for that... and I have nothing but respect for you.
So please... don't talk about yourself that way.
If Onisaka-san knew about this, I'm sure he'd forgive you for going back on your word. You still haven't told him about the accident, right?
No. I didn't want to use my wife as an excuse. And I just couldn't face up to him.
I'm a former racer myself, so I know exactly how he feels. I know how much he wants that rematch.
Yeah, but...
If I told him about the accident, sure, he'd probably let it slide.
But think about what that'd do to him. Cars have been his life. I don't wanna ruin that for him.
I don't think tellin' him's a good idea.
So you want Onisaka to keep on racing, then?
I used to want that. I figured with me off the road, he might as well do enough racin' for the both of us.
But now I don't know. He's gettin' old. I don't want him chained to this life until it's too late. One day he'll push it too far.
And when he bows out, I want it to be at the right time... I don't want him to end up like me.
Now, if someone were to beat him in a race, maybe that'd give him what he needs to lay his pride down...
Then that's what I'll do.
I'll challenge Onisaka-san and put an end to his career.
You'd... You'd do that?
Sure. Back when I was lost, you gave me a place and a purpose. That's always meant a lot to me... so let me pay you back.
But that's askin' too much...
Nakajima-san, listen. I've taken down all the Devil Killers. And now I'm the fastest in Fukuoka, just like you were.
It's my turn to step up and race in your stead. You leave this to me.
...Thank you.
You got 2,400 experience points.
We had another call from that Onisaka-san fellow. He's asking for the chief again...
(I have to beat Onisaka this time, and get him to retire from racing!)
I'll go in his place.
Go get 'em, Suzuki-san!
Break a leg out there.
We'll be rooting for you.
Drive safely now!
Thanks. Here goes nothing...
Hmm. This is a call from someone named Onisaka-san. But he's requested the chief, out of all people...
I'll be taking that job.
I'm not sure that's such a good idea...
Normally I'd agree, but the chief is out right now. Might as well let him do it, Hirakawa-san.
True, it isn't like we have another option... Okay then. Suzuki-san, he's all yours. Thanks for volunteering.
It's been a long uphill battle since you first ran into the Devil Killers. But once you do this, it'll all be over at last.
Make sure you win, so Onisaka can finally get some peace of mind.
Be careful out there. We all know you've got what it takes.
Yeah! Carve your own destiny, man! No matter how tough the challenge, there's nothing you can't do!
Heh, you guys... Thanks.
Guess I'll be heading out now.
Go get 'em!
See you later.

en: Have a nice trip!
How many times do I gotta tell ya? It's Nakajima I want to race. A bum like you could never fill his shoes!
Or do you actually think you have a chance of winning this time? That stubborn streak does remind me of Nakajima, back in the day...
Heh, all right then. I'll give you another shot. Get in your car!
Hey, I asked for Nakajima, not you.
I thought you wanted the thrill of going up against the top racer in Fukuoka.
No need to bother Nakajima-san if that's what you're looking for. I'm your man.
Heh... Heheh... Hahahahaha!
What's so funny?
Sorry. It just seems you're lettin' the fact you took down the Devil Killers go to your head.
I'm saying you can't live up to Nakajima's legacy.
I saw you race Takamura. You're nowhere near Nakajima's level.
Taking you on would be like arm-wrestling a baby! Not that I suggest that, but you get the picture.
You got some weak-ass odds, my friend. Might as well head on back in that taxi of yours!
The odds aren't what's important. As long as there's a chance, I'll take it.
I can see you're letting the past hold you back. I'm here to change that.
...Interesting. No wonder Nakajima hired you on.
Fine, you'll get your shot. But fair warning... I got twenty years of pure rage in this beating heart of mine, and I'm takin' it out on you!
Talk about a snail's pace! And you think you can stand in for Nakajima!? Don't make me laugh!
Next time, bring that president of yours. And leave that cab at the office!
You really did it, huh... You beat me.
I suppose I did.
Heheh...Heh...Hahahahahaaa!
(What now?)

This! This is the thrill I've been looking for! I feel like
I'm alive again!
I've been waiting so long just to feel it... one more time.
Ya did good, Suzuki-san. Thank you.
It was almost like racing against the man himself...
The guy I've been chasing all these years.
...I'm sorry, Onisaka.
Nakajima!?
I know I disappeared on ya, but... I couldn't...
Don't say another word. I know how hard it is.
Even so, the way I went about it... I got no excuse.
Don't sweat it. We're all good, man.
(...So the rivals are reunited at last. Seems like they're off to a good start.)
An accident? That's terrible...
Still... Wish things didn't end the way they did.
Mm. I figured it was along those lines. It'd have to be something major to get you to quit.
...I appreciate yer understanding.
Well, I can't say I'm not disappointed. I never did get my rematch.
But going up against Suzuki-san here got all that anger out of my system. I think it's time I finally left the racing life behind.
...Ya mean that?
Yeah. In all honesty, I just wanted to go out on a high. One last race was all I needed.
And thanks to you, I got it.
...You're a good man, Suzuki-san.
Heh. Guess I made the right call.
Furumichi-san? You're here too?
Well, aren't you a sight for sore eyes.
You know each other?
'Course we do.
Furumichi here was one of the Three Musketeers. Can you believe this goody two-shoes was a street racer!?
Is this true?
Haha, what? An honest cop can't have a bit of a past? Though I'd really rather you not dig that up...
No, it's just that... I never would've expected you to be involved. Especially with a group like the Devil Killers.
Sorry to keep that little detail a secret. What with my current position, I'm reluctant to talk about my history. I'm sure you understand.
At any rate, you've done a fine job here. I'll say it again⑬nice work, Suzuki-san. And thank you.
Thanks to you, the Devil Killers are no more, and our old ties are mended.
I'd give you a commendation if I could... but that's a bit tricky, considering the methods we used.
Your thanks is more than enough.
No, I can't just leave it at that. Here, take this. It's no commendation, but it'll have to do.
You got <Color:8>Sakura Storm<Color:Default>.

Well, how 'bout that? The Three Musketeers, together again.
How about we catch up over drinks tonight?
Sounds like a plan.
Your treat, Furumichi?
What? I thought it'd be on the "chief" here!
Huh!? Why me?
(Well, I took down what was left of the Devil Killers, and repaired an old friendship. It was a long road, but it was well worth it.)
Hey, Suzuki-san! How'd it go? Did you beat Onisaka?
I managed to win somehow.
Awesome! Way to go, Suzuki-san!
Well, that's good news, isn't it? Now you won't get people trying to race you left and right.
